text:
Neal Pionk has 14 points in 24 games for Winnipeg, two more than he had in 51 games last season. For a 31-year-old defenseman coming off a year Evolving-Hockey graded at replacement level, that is a genuine bounce.

The underlying work explains most of it. His individual expected goals per 60 has doubled, 0.21 last season to 0.42 now, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man even in the down year (5.5 primary shot assists per 60, 81st percentile among defensemen). He is shooting 7.7%, only a hair above his talent range, and Winnipeg has actually scored 4.7 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, which has cost him points.

The worry is the other end. Winnipeg is getting only 47% of the 5v5 expected goals with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey's note from last season says chances against piled up with him on (bottom 8% of defensemen) while he faced the other team's best. At 24:17 a night, that defensive side matters as much as the points.
headline: Neal Pionk's offense is back, and it is mostly real
